results.title: Choosing the Right Heroku Postgres Plan | Heroku Dev Center
results.content:
## Essential Tier

The Essential tier includes the `essential-0`, `essential-1`, and `essential-2` plans. This tier has the following limitations:

- No fork and follow support: Fork and follow, used to create replica databases and leader-follower setups, aren’t supported.
- No Expensive Queries support
- Expected uptime of 99.5% each month
- Unannounced maintenance and automatic Postgres version upgrades
- No Postgres logs
- No additional credentials

If you get the error `The authentication type 10 is not supported.` or `SCRAM authentication is not supported by this driver.` while connecting to your Essential database, see this Help article.

The plans for the Essentials tier are:

| Plan Name | Provisioning Name | Limits | Storage | Connection Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Essential-0 | `heroku-postgresql:essential-0` | 4,000 tables | 1 GB | 20 |
| Essential-1 | `heroku-postgresql:essential-1` | 4,000 tables | 10 GB | 20 |
| Essential-2 | `heroku-postgresql:essential-2` | 4,000 tables | 32 GB | 40 |

results.title: Free Heroku Dynos, Heroku Postgres and Heroku Data for Redis are no longer available | Heroku Dev Center
results.content:
# Free Heroku Dynos, Heroku Postgres and Heroku Data for Redis are no longer available

 Change effective on 28 November 2022 

As of November 28th, 2022, Heroku is no longer offering `free` dynos, `hobby-dev` Heroku Postgres, or `hobby-dev` Heroku Data for Redis plans.

- Heroku has started converting existing `free` dynos to `eco` dynos and scaling them to 0. You must subscribe to Eco or upgrade to another paid plan to get your app running again.
- We have started queuing existing `hobby-dev` databases in personal and Heroku Team accounts for deletion.
- We have started converting existing `hobby-dev` databases belonging to Enterprise Accounts to `mini` plans.

See our blog post announcement and FAQs for more info.
